Subject: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend vs surge fees?

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataWave's ML infra and product team are excited about Redwood's latency profile. I'm pulling together a cost model for our 2027 roadmap and need clarity on two things before we get procurement involved:

1) Minimum monthly/annual commit requirements for the hosted API. Do you have a standard minimum (floor) or is that negotiated per-deal?
2) How do you price on-demand overages when traffic spikes above the commit? Specifically: is there a single overage rate, are there tiered surcharges, or a soft-burst allowance?

For context, our rough profile is: baseline ~100M tokens/month for product reads/writes, but we expect occasional spikes up to ~300M tokens in heavy campaign periods (1-3 days). We want to understand expected unit economics under a 12-month contract vs pay-as-you-go.

Can you share an example cost table (commit tiers, per-token discounts, overage pricing, and any true-up cadence)? Also include any options for a capped monthly spend or grace buffer during onboarding.

If useful, I'll loop James (procurement) in on follow-ups.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Head of Product

Hi Anna — great to hear and thanks for the clear context. Below is a concise breakdown of how Redwood typically structures Hosted API pricing for usage-based deals; I'll attach a worked example for your 100M baseline / 300M spike profile.

High-level model (hosted API):
- Unit pricing: per-token (billed per 1k tokens). We publish a base on-demand unit rate, and committed tiers receive stepped discounts off that rate.
- Commit floor (minimum monthly billing): negotiated per-account; common starting point for enterprise pilots is a $10k/month floor for 12-months, but we can adjust for scale and strategic deals. Floors are credit-backed and amortized across the year.
- Burst policy: soft burst buffer + on-demand overage: customers receive a configurable soft buffer (we recommend 25% of committed throughput) that can be used without a surge surcharge for short periods. Beyond that buffer, traffic falls back to on-demand pricing at a higher per-token rate (on-demand = 1.15x base rate in the example sheet). For sustained overages, we have a monthly true-up and an optional quarterly true-up flow.
- Overage tiers: we can tier on-demand overage rates (e.g., 0-50% above buffer = 1.15x, 50-150% above buffer = 1.35x) for larger spikes — this is negotiable by deal.
- Ramp and credits: for onboarding we can provide a 30-day grace period where the soft buffer is temporarily increased (we sometimes provide a one-time 50% buffer for month 1–2 to cover load testing).

Example (see attached 'pricing-worksheet-DataWave-100M-300M.xlsx'):
- Baseline commit example: 100M tokens/month committed at a committed rate 0.00075 USD per token (example).
- Soft buffer: 25% (i.e., 25M tokens) allowed above the 100M committed at the committed unit rate.
- Above buffer: on-demand rate = 0.00086 USD per token (1.15x).
- Heavy spike band (>125M): surge band billed at 1.35x committed rate (0.00101 USD/token) — applied to the portion of usage in that band.
- True-up: monthly reconciliation with quarterly settlement for material overages (>20% variance sustained).

Contracting levers we commonly use:
- Commit size and term (12 vs 24 months) — longer terms reduce unit price and lower the floor.
- Burst buffer size and one-time onboarding buffers.
- Cap on monthly invoice (we can add a soft cap with notice + throttle option instead of unlimited exposure).
- SLA credits and custom support — included in enterprise packages.

Next steps: I'll attach a modeled worksheet with numbers populated to match your 100M baseline and a 300M spike. If you want, we can propose two options: (A) lower minimum/month with slightly higher committed unit price, or (B) a stronger discount for a higher, 12-month committed floor. Lauren is cc'd and can draft a formal proposal once you confirm which direction you prefer.

Thanks Ben — that helps a lot. A few clarifying items from procurement:

- Our purchasing team is comfortable with a 12-month term but wants the monthly minimum to be no higher than $12k to preserve runway during Q1. Would you be able to do a 12-month commit with that floor?
- Request for a monthly invoice cap option (with a notification threshold) — we want an automated throttle option rather than surprise invoices if we see an unexpected multi-day spike.
- EU data residency: some of our user data is EU-first. Are there any pricing adjustments for using regional endpoints?

If you can send a redlineable proposal (SOW + pricing) that includes (a) a 12-month option at a $12k/mo floor and (b) an alternative 12-month option with a $18k/mo floor + stronger discounts, that will speed procurement review. Please include expected SLA credits for availability <99.9% and the proposed true-up cadence.

Anna — thanks for the clear ask. I've worked with Ben and finance to draft two practical options that map to your procurement ask. Summary below and I've attached a redline-friendly SOW + Master Sales Terms. If either option looks good, we can push a DocuSign packet and copy your procurement team.

Option A — Conservative commit (aligns with $12k/mo floor):
- Term: 12 months
- Minimum monthly spend (floor): $12,000
- Committed baseline: 100M tokens/month (amortized across term)
- Committed unit rate: 0.00080 USD/token
- Soft burst buffer: 20% of committed capacity/month (for brief spikes)
- Overage: on-demand billing at 1.20x committed rate for usage beyond buffer; monthly true-up
- Onboarding grace: first 60 days include a one-time temporary buffer increase to 50% (no surge surcharge)
- Invoice cap option: added — with automatic throttle feature and notification threshold at 85% of cap
- SLA: availability credit schedule included in SOW (credit starts at <99.9%)

Option B — Higher commit, stronger discounts (aligns with $18k/mo floor):
- Term: 12 months
- Minimum monthly spend (floor): $18,000
- Committed baseline: 150M tokens/month
- Committed unit rate: 0.00066 USD/token (approx. 17% discount vs Option A)
- Soft burst buffer: 30% of committed capacity/month
- Overage: tiered on-demand bands (0-30% above buffer = 1.10x; 30-100% = 1.30x)
- Onboarding grace: first 90 days with elevated buffer and one-time credit for unexpected testing costs
- Invoice cap and throttle available
- SLA: higher tier SLA credits and a named technical account manager included

EU data residency: we can attach regional endpoints for EU traffic; pricing is unchanged for routing to Redwood's EU-hosted clusters for standard usage, but for dedicated private deployments there may be additional hosting fees (we've noted that in the SOW).

- I attached: Master-Sales-Terms-Redwood.pdf, SOW-DataWave-hosted-api-draft.docx, and a populated pricing worksheet.
- If either option looks acceptable, reply with preferred option and we'll send DocuSign (link included). We're prepared to add a monthly invoice cap with throttle override terms to the SOW.
